summary: Session-model-lease expiry leads to opaque reroute to compatibility variant
description:
Issue summary: ScribeFlow reported intermittent production requests returning responses from their compatibility model (redwood-compat-v1.8) despite having a tenant-scoped model pin to redwood-rlhf-v2.0-q4_0. The routing change is opaque to the client and appears correlated with long-lived streaming sessions.

Impact: Customer observed ~2% of requests in the last 24h routed to the compatibility variant during steady traffic (500-700 rps). This caused subtle output differences for a small percentage of calls and triggered quality alerts in the customer's monitoring. No tokens or billing discrepancies reported yet; customer wants guaranteed pin preservation for their dedicated pool.

Environment: production - dedicated cluster in us-east-1. Tenant: scribeflow-prod, dedicated capacity pool id dc-73.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Initiate a long streaming conversation using the tenant API key with model selection set to redwood-rlhf-v2.0-q4_0 and tenant model pin enabled.
2) Maintain an open stream for >1200s with intermittent small requests (keepalives + short messages).
3) During sustained prewarm/autoscaler activity (scale-up of dc-73), some subsequent requests in the same session are routed to redwood-compat-v1.8.

Observed logs and snippets:
- Edge logs show session-lease-refresh succeeded at T+600s but lease TTL reported 0 in the orchestrator snapshot at T+1210s.
- Orchestrator debug: "session_lease_reconcile: lease_expired TRUE for tenant scribeflow-prod, last_seen=2026-03-12T11:04:08Z"
- Serving-runtime route decision: "selected_variant=compat-v1.8, reason=fallback_policy:lease_expired"

Immediate hypothesis: Session-model-lease TTL is being truncated during orchestrator snapshot merges when a scaling event interleaves prewarm requests. The edge/session-store (Redis) shows the lease key still present, but the orchestrator's in-memory snapshot marks it expired due to a TTL conversion bug when merging epoch-aligned snapshots from two orchestrator replicas. That causes a short-lived but opaque reroute to a compatibility variant via the fallback policy.

Potential customer-visible cause: Requests inside the same streaming session see a variant flip because the routing decision consults the orchestrator snapshot first and only falls back to session-store after a short timeout; that race window currently allows an immediate fallback.

Logs/links:
- Edge request id 7f3a2a4b - link to trace: https://traces.redwoodinc/trace/7f3a2a4b
- Orchestrator snapshot dump: s3://redwood-debug/dumps/dc-73/snapshot-2026-03-12-11-05.json (internal)

Recommended next steps (initial):
- Engineering to reproduce in staging with controlled autoscaler prewarm/scale events and long streaming sessions.
- Add additional defensive reconciliation: prefer authoritative session-store TTL if snapshot reports expired and session-store reports active, during a short grace window.
- Instrument TTL conversion codepaths in orchestrator snapshot merge.

Investigation notes:
- Repro run in staging succeeded: we reproduced variant flip when orchestrator snapshot merge coincided with a replica rejoin after GC pause.
- Root cause narrowed to a signed/unsigned integer conversion in seconds->ms TTL math in orchestrator merge that produced negative TTL for leases older than ~2^31 seconds in rare timestamp scenarios (observed during replica clock skew + GC).
- Workaround implemented in-staging: apply +grace-window (5s) in routing decision and re-query session-store when snapshot shows lease expired for active streaming sessions.

Business/CS notes:
- Customer notified 2026-03-12 14:20 UTC, asked for timeframe for full fix and whether a hotfix is available.
- Customer requests confirmation that tenant pins will be preserved during dedicated autoscale events.

Resolution notes (work in progress):
- Short-term mitigation: rolled out routing grace window to dc-73 rollback group 1 (affects ~20% of traffic) on 2026-03-13 02:30 UTC. Early telemetry shows variant flips reduced to <0.1%.
- Engineering PR in review to fix TTL conversion and add unit tests for negative TTL edge cases.
- Plan for full rollout to all dedicated pools after validation in staging and canary (expected 48-72h after PR merge).
